title: Bishop laments ASEAN protest arrests on World Day of the Poor
summary: "Poverty is not a crime," a bishop says, noting the irony of arrests of those raising concerns about communities and livelihoods.

blocks.text: Protesters clash with police officers during a demonstration that coincides with the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Leaders' Summit and Related Summits in Manila on Nov. 15, 2026.

MANILA, Philippines — The Catholic Church was observing the World Day of the Poor when hundreds of Filipinos were arrested during the ASEAN summit protests on Sunday, November 15, San Carlos Bishop Gerardo Alminaza said.

The bishop pointed to the irony on Tuesday, saying the arrests came as protesters were raising concerns about their rights, livelihoods and communities, underscoring the need to protect the voices of marginalized Filipinos.

"Poverty is not a crime. Peaceful protest is not a crime. Demanding justice is not a crime," Alminaza said in a statement Tuesday, November 17. "The poor deserve a seat at the table and a meaningful voice in decisions that shape their future."
More than 300 people were reportedly arrested during demonstrations across Metro Manila as Southeast Asian leaders gathered for the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit.

Alminaza urged the Commission on Human Rights (CHR) and other independent bodies to investigate reports of police abuse during the November 15 protests, including incidents involving journalists and a reported arrest on church property.
He also called on authorities to preserve evidence, allow independent access to detainees and hold personnel accountable for any violations.

"Authorities have a responsibility to protect public safety. That responsibility must be exercised with restraint and respect for human dignity. Allegations against particular individuals must be examined fairly; they must never become a blanket justification for punishing peaceful dissent," Alminaza said.
The bishop demanded the immediate release of those detained solely for exercising their right to peaceful assembly and the withdrawal of charges based only on such activities.

"I call for the immediate release of all those detained solely for peacefully exercising their rights, and for the withdrawal of charges based solely on such exercise. Every person in custody must have prompt access to legal counsel, family members and necessary medical care. Children must receive appropriate care, protection and assistance, with their best interests given priority," he said.

The Philippine National Police has defended its handling of the demonstrations, saying officers exercised maximum tolerance and that arrests were made in response to alleged obstruction of public roads and refusals to comply with authorities.
